title: Radial-kernel mean value identity implies the open-ball mean value identity
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, h : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = Euclid n), x ∈ ℝⁿ and r > 0, with h continuous on closedBall(x, r). Assume that for every continuous g : ℝ → ℝ with g(t) = 0 for all t ≥ r², ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(x − y)·g(|y|²) dy = h(x)·∫_{ℝⁿ} g(|y|²) dy. Then ∫_{B̆_r(x)} h = Lⁿ(B̆_r(x))·h(x). Here B̆_r(x) = ball(x, r) is the open ball, Lⁿ = volume is Lebesgue measure, and the measure is taken as a real number via ENNReal.toReal.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (x : Euclid n) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ContinuousOn h (closedBall x r) → (∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, Continuous g → (∀ t : ℝ, r ^ 2 ≤ t → g t = 0) → ∫ y : Euclid n, h (x - y) * g (‖y‖ ^ 2) = h x * ∫ y : Euclid n, g (‖y‖ ^ 2)) → ∫ y in ball x r, h y = (volume (ball x r)).toReal * h x
